title: Ultrasound-guided blocks for the hip and femur: femoral, fascia iliaca and PENG
short: Blocks for hip and femoral fractures
summary: A fractured neck of femur is the commonest serious injury in older people, and a nerve block on arrival is part of good care. Learn the femoral nerve block, the infra-inguinal and supra-inguinal fascia iliaca blocks and the PENG block: the anatomy, the safety system, how to choose between them and the evidence.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency and acute care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and nurses who perform, or are training to perform, ultrasound-guided blocks for hip and femoral fractures under their trust's governance.
outcomes: Explain why early nerve blocks matter in hip fracture, and summarise the evidence
Set up a safe block in a frail patient: capacity, dose calculation, monitoring, Stop Before You Block and documentation
Perform the sonoanatomy and needle path for the femoral nerve, infra-inguinal and supra-inguinal fascia iliaca and PENG blocks
Choose between the blocks for a given injury and patient
Recognise the risks of each block, including quadriceps weakness and local anaesthetic toxicity
